newsitem.title: CHINA: Deng Xiaoping - a man of many deeds -- and names.
newsitem.headline: Deng Xiaoping - a man of many deeds -- and names.

text.p: His name meant "little peace", which in Chinese rhymes with "little bottle", but that was only one of several Deng Xiaoping name games.
Little he certainly was: he stood just over five feet (152 cm) tall. Peace hardly did justice to his tumultuous life and times.

Yet in a language that lends itself to rhymes and puns, Xiaoping also sounds like "little bottle". To show their anger at Deng after the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre, but without breaking any law, Chinese students craftily smashed beer and soft drink bottles.
Deng Xiaoping was one of at least three names the Sichuan province native used in life.
He was born Xixian, or "hope of the virtuous", which became the single name Bin, "refined", a nomme de guerre during the civil war with the Chinese Nationalists in the 1920s.
The switch to "Xiaoping" came in 1927 when as a 23-year-old revolutionary he followed the communist party to its secret headquarters in Shanghai.
Along the way there were colourful nicknames: during his student years in France, Deng's communist comrades dubbed the fiery organiser "little cannon".
There were plenty of sobriquets too, not all of them flattering. Henry Kissinger famously called him a "nasty little man".
